name: Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport
before:
One of the three big Pearl River Delta airports, alongside Hong Kong and Guangzhou Baiyun. It is on the east bank of the Pearl River in Bao'an District, 32 km north west of central Shenzhen, and it is a hub for Shenzhen Airlines, China Southern and Donghai Airlines, with UPS running its Asia Pacific cargo hub here.

The detail most people miss is the ferry. There are direct sailings to Hong Kong International Airport and passengers transit without clearing immigration and customs, which can turn an awkward two airport itinerary into a simple one.

On land the Ground Transportation Centre sits a short walk from baggage reclaim. Long distance and local buses use the first floor, taxis and the Airport Express 330 the second, and the underground level connects to Airport Station on Metro Line 11, which runs east to Futian for high speed rail.

Capacity keeps growing. A second runway opened in 2011, a new terminal in 2013 and a third runway in November 2025.
after:
One of the three big Pearl River Delta airports, alongside Hong Kong and Guangzhou Baiyun. It is in Bao'an District, 32 km north west of central Shenzhen.

Shenzhen Airlines has its hub here and Donghai Airlines its main base. China Southern also has a big presence, and UPS runs a cargo hub.

Buses leave from the Ground Transportation Centre, and Metro Line 11 stops at the airport.

A second runway opened in 2011, a new terminal in 2013 and a third runway in November 2025.

claims.claim: direct ferries to HKIA, transit without immigration
claims.wasBefore: There are direct sailings to Hong Kong International Airport and passengers transit without clearing immigration and customs
claims.why: Sources conflict on whether it still runs. HKIA's own page still lists Shenzhen Fuyong among its SkyPier ports, but Shenzhen Bendibao's June 2026 timetable lists only Macau Taipa, Guishan and Dong'ao from the airport pier, and search results quote the operator's timetable page as suspending the Hong Kong airport sailings from 16 March 2026 (that page could not be saved). The wording was also loose: passengers do clear Chinese immigration and customs, once, at Fuyong.
